items.title: D.C.N.E.
items.decryption: D: Dukkha (Suffering), C: Cause (Samudaya), N: Nirodha (Cessation), E: Eightfold Path (Magga - the remedy).

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Thinking the 4 Noble Truths are the same as the Eightfold Path (The Truths are the diagnosis, the Path is the prescription).
Assuming Nirvana is explicitly defined in the 4 Truths; it is the implicit 'end state' of the third truth (Nirodha).

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Context

  • Location: Deer Park, Sarnath
  • Audience: The Five Ascetics
  • Scripture: Vinaya Pitaka

Core Elements

  • Dukkha: Universal suffering
  • Samudaya: Origin (Tanha)
  • Nirodha: Elimination
  • Magga: The Path

Core Philosophical Structure

  • 1. Dukkha (Suffering): Life is characterized by suffering; birth, decay, disease, and death are inescapable.
  • 2. Samudaya (Origin of Suffering): The root cause is 'Tanha' (desire/craving), fueled by ignorance (Avidya).
  • 3. Nirodha (Cessation): Suffering can be extinguished by eliminating desire; this leads to Nirvana.
  • 4. Magga (The Path): The Ashtangika Marga (Eightfold Path) provides the practical method to achieve cessation.
Truth (Arya Satya)Significance
DukkhaReality of life
SamudayaRoot cause (Tanha)
NirodhaPotential for liberation
MaggaMeans to liberation
